az_bug_spring_wall.blurb: Bug Spring Wall is a small granite crag on the lower slopes of Mount Lemmon, north of Tucson, in the Catalina Highway climbing zone. It holds 18 routes split evenly between bolted lines and gear climbs, spread over an east and a west face. Grades run from 5.7 to 5.10, with the middle grades most common, which suits climbers working through the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The rock is mostly solid, with horizontal cracks giving both holds and protection and a few small loose patches. The main wall looks northwest, so mornings tend to be cool and shaded. The walk in is an adventure of its own, through a wash with boulder hopping, so it sees fewer people than the roadside crags.

az_west_face.blurb: West Face is a wall on the Druid formation in the mid-mountain zone of Mount Lemmon, high in the Santa Catalina Mountains above Tucson, among ponderosa pines at roughly 7,800 feet. It has 18 climbs, mostly short bolted lines plus some gear routes, one aid line and a couple of top-rope options. Difficulty runs from easy fifth class up through the low 5.11s, with the bulk of routes between 5.8 and 5.10. A few climbs run two pitches. Being up in the forest, it is a cooler escape from the desert heat below, though dead trees from an old burn nearby are worth watching for.

az_the_iron_wall.blurb: The Iron Wall sits on the south side of Volunteer Canyon inside Sycamore Canyon, west of Flagstaff, among ponderosa pine forest. Every one of its 18 routes is a gear climb on well-formed basalt columns. Grades start around 5.9 and climb to 5.13, with a tight cluster of 5.10s and 5.11s making it useful as a warm-up spot as well as a place for hard test pieces. True beginners will find very little here. The wall faces northwest and keeps its shade until early afternoon, which helps on warm days. Routes are reached by rappelling in, so finding them the first time takes some patience.

az_fortress_the.blurb: The Fortress is a formation of around 150 feet in the Superstition Mountains east of Phoenix, with west and south faces looking over the Peralta Trail and broad views across the range. It mixes traditional routes, a pair of bolted lines and a set of boulder problems, 18 climbs in all. Roped climbs go from easy fifth class to the low 5.11s, while the problems range from moderate up to a few seriously hard lines in the V8 to V10 territory. Most of the range is wilderness where new bolting is not done, so expect a gear-oriented, adventurous feel and a long hike in.

az_wiley_thompson_boulder.blurb: Wiley Thompson Boulder is one of the best-known blocks at Beardsley, a desert bouldering area on the north edge of Phoenix. It sits right beside the main trail and is easy to spot, and many first-time visitors start here. The 18 problems are all bouldering, ranging from VB-level warm-ups through the V3 to V4 middle and up to about V7. Holds are good with some tiny crimps, landings are flat, and the top-out has an easy walk-off, so it works well for mixed groups. Expect coarse, weathered granite and bring a pad for the taller lines.

az_upper_wall_2.blurb: Upper Wall is the better of the walls at Raycreation, a small area high on Mount Lemmon above Tucson at about 7,600 feet. All 18 routes are bolted, rising to roughly 50 feet on steep, juggy faces. Grades span 5.7 to 5.12, but the heart of the wall is 5.10 and 5.11, so it favours climbers comfortable leading in that range. The rock can be grainy with some lichen. It faces west-northwest, giving afternoon sun, and the cool elevation makes it a popular summer retreat. Expect company on weekends and quiet on weekdays.

az_zappa_dome.blurb: Zappa Dome is a south-facing sport wall on the east side of Cochise Stronghold in the Dragoon Mountains of southeast Arizona. It carries 18 bolted single-pitch routes on a solid, fairly clean face, though a few spots are flaky. Most climbs fall between 5.9 and 5.10, with a handful of easier and harder options including one easy 5.5, so it suits intermediate climbers well. Warm sun and little shade make it a good winter choice and a hot place in summer. The walk up from the small lot below the neighbouring dome is a cairned trail of about twenty minutes.
